statement.essentials: An alternative incision, borrowed from facelift surgery, hides the scar in front of and behind the ear and in the hairline instead of in the neck.
statement.anatomy: The modified facelift incision follows the edge of the tragus to the earlobe, passes round the lobule and runs up behind the ear toward the hairline. It avoids a neck scar and gives adequate exposure for selected tumours, which are mostly small, mobile and benign.
statement.clinical: In a meta-analysis of seven studies of presumed benign tumours the facelift incision scored higher for cosmetic satisfaction and caused less Frey syndrome, with similar rates of facial palsy and salivary complications; operations took somewhat longer and the tumours were smaller. One series used it only for benign, mobile tumours under 4 cm and found tumours at the far periphery, and the upper neck nodes, not always reachable.

limitations: Observational comparisons: the facelift incision went to smaller, more benign tumours in surgeons who chose it. A narrative review notes that well-designed prospective studies are lacking and that these incisions remain largely with experienced surgeons at high-volume centres. The path drawn in the model is one representative facelift-type incision.
